transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood), Ana Ruiz (CTO, Edgecraft), Marcus Li (ML Eng), Sophie Grant (Head of Product), Tom Brooks (SRE, joined later)

Summary: quick scoping call focused on model choice for multilingual customer-support assistant, context length requirements (long-doc summarization & RAG), and evaluation of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) deployments. Team requested benchmark template and pricing comparison; agreed to deeper technical session with SRE to validate VPC connectivity and KMS flows.

Topics covered: open-model tradeoffs, 50k+ context needs, multilingual (es/ja/fr), tool-calling for vector search + external PDF parser, privacy/residency needs, SSO/KMS, latency vs cost, rollout plan (canary + fallback).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Liam. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ana: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in. We're pretty timeboxed, we wanted to get through model choice and deployment options.
[00:11] Marcus: Yep, and to be clear we have a production timeline we want to hit—Q4 pilot internal, production next Q1.
[00:18] Jared: Great. Can you give a quick rundown of the main workload? Sophie?
[00:23] Sophie: Sure. Edgecraft runs support for multiple content verticals — video metadata, ad ops, creator community. We want an assistant that can ingest long transcripts and docs (one-off transcripts, contracts) and answer multi-turn queries. Language mix is mostly English and Spanish, but we have a small Japan & French user base. Latency target for interactive use is sub-500ms p50 on the host path, but for long-doc summarization batch can be slower. Cost is a big factor — we run millions of tokens a month.
[00:44] Priya: Thanks. A couple clarifying q's: what do you mean by long docs — expected token lengths, and do you need the model to hold a full 50k context or are you ok with RAG + 8k/16k model for short turn and a separate long-context path?
[00:58] Marcus: We have transcripts that can be 30–60 pages. So want a single query to reference sections across a doc. Ideally 50k would be nice. We also had thought about chunking, but that adds complexity and hits quality.
[01:12] Tom (via chat later): Also we need to keep PII out of hosted logs and want KMS-backed encryption, and SSO for access.
[01:20] Priya: Understood. On the model side, there's a few axes — model family (open Llama-style vs Mistral/Mosaic/Meta), quantization and tokenization behaviour, latency per token, and currently Redwood supports routes for Hosted (fast to spin up), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem). We often recommend a hybrid: hosted for dev & non-sensitive traffic, dedicated or private for PII-sensitive production.
[01:43] Ana: What's the gap between dedicated and private — is private basically full VPC control?
[01:47] Jared: Private gives you customer-managed network, optional on-prem, and a private control plane so logs and control are within your network. Dedicated is still run by Redwood in our infra but isolated GPU pools and committed capacity. For strict residency or air-gapped requirements you'd look at private.
[02:02] Sophie: For our compliance team, SOC2 is fine, but they want KMS and audit logs, possibly HSM.
[02:09] Priya: We have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM options) and per-request audit logs you can retain in your storage. We'll share the security pack.
[02:18] Marcus: On model selection: we looked at Llama 3 variants, Mistral Large and some 70B mosaics. We're concerned about hallucinations on long-context. Do you do quantization-friendly runs?
[02:31] Priya: Yes — there's a tradeoff. Larger dense models with 32-bit compute give best quality, but higher cost. 8-bit/4-bit quantization helps cost but can slightly change generation characteristics. Our runtime optimizes kernels and KV-cache to reduce token amplification. For long context, we support some specialized long-attention variants and can stitch LV models for longer context windows with caching.
[02:50] Marcus: Stitch LV?
[02:51] Priya: Sorry, I mean stitching a long-context adapter — conceptually you can have a model with native 64k context or use retrieval-augmented strategies with cache to approximate. We also have prefix/KV caching so repeated queries are faster.
[03:03] Ana: On multilinguality — do models handle Spanish and Japanese out of the box, or do you recommend fine-tuning?
[03:09] Priya: Many open models are multilingual out of the box but vary. For Spanish, most Llama-derivatives and Mistral do okay. For Japanese, you might need a model with Japanese tokens in tokenizer or a fine-tuned variant. We can run evals on your sample data.
[03:24] Sophie: We want to support code-switching queries (Spanglish), so tokenization matters.
[03:28] Priya: Agree — tokenizer overlap is important. We'll add that to the eval matrix.
[03:32] Jared: Talking about tool-calling — what external tools do you need? We saw notes about an internal search service, PDF extractor, and a connector to your CRM.
[03:41] Marcus: Yes. We want tool-calling to: 1) run vector search against our index, 2) call a PDF parsing microservice for long documents, 3) optionally call a small business-rules microservice to redact PII. Latency for tool-call round-trip should be <200ms ideally.
[03:59] Priya: Redwood supports function/tool calling primitives and structured responses. For latency-sensitive paths we recommend colocating tool endpoints in same region and using caching. For the PDF parser, batching works for large jobs. For interactive tool-call, we can set up dedicated pools with fast network egress.
[04:16] Ana: Any concerns about cost if we run long-context native models?
[04:19] Jared: Native 50k contexts do increase compute per inference—cost scales roughly with tokens processed. We can quantify with a benchmark. That's where Dedicated with reserved capacity and autoscaling policies can reduce unit cost versus Hosted. Also quantization and batching reduce cost.
[04:34] Sophie: Can we mix models by route? Like low-cost small model for general queries, high-cost long-context model for guaranteed doc lookups?
[04:41] Priya: Absolutely — routing policies can send requests to model variants by route or content type. We also support automatic fallback to cheaper or higher-availability variants. Can do A/B rollouts.
[04:51] Marcus: For evaluation, what would you need from us to run a representative benchmark?
[04:54] Priya: A sample corpus (transcripts/PDFs), 50–100 representative queries across languages, desired latency targets, and peak QPS. We'll run per-token latency, end-to-end p50/p95, and quality metrics (exact match / F1 / ROI). We'll share the benchmark template.
[05:12] Ana: About compliance, how do logs work for Hosted? We can't have PII stored in Redwood logs.
[05:18] Jared: For Hosted, logs are within Redwood unless you enable Private or set up log forwarding to your storage. We can scrub PII at ingestion, and enable request-level opt-outs. For full control, Private with customer-managed control plane is recommended.
[05:32] Tom: (joined) Sorry for the delay, quick Q — how does VPC peering work? We have strict firewall rules.
[05:38] Liam: We do VPC peering and private endpoints, and we can work with your network team to open minimal egress. We'll provide diagrams and a runbook for peering.
[05:47] Tom: Good. Also curious about SAML + RBAC for console access.
[05:50] Jared: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and granular RBAC. We'll share an example policy.
[05:56] Sophie: Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[05:58] Priya: A few: 1) Tokenization mismatches across model checkpoints can change outputs; be explicit in evals. 2) Long-context models may have higher p95 latency. 3) Tool-calling retries need idempotency. 4) Data residency — ensure you pick Private or region pinning if required.
[06:18] Marcus: On hallucinations, do you do guardrails or evaluation for hallucination rates?
[06:22] Priya: We measure hallucination on benchmark prompts and track quality regressions via Evaluate/Optimize. We can also set up reranking or calibrator layers that check answers against retrieved evidence.
[06:34] Ana: Ok next steps — we'd like the benchmark template and a pricing worksheet. We'll produce the sample datasets.
[06:39] Jared: Sounds good. Priya, anything to add?
[06:41] Priya: I'll include the template and a list of suggested models to test — we recommend testing a 70B dense, a 13–34B quantized variant, and a native long-context variant if you need 50k. Also I'll include a shepherded runbook for the technical deep dive.
[06:58] Sophie: Perfect. Schedule the SRE deep dive and we'll gather logs for Marcus to upload.
[07:03] Jared: I'll follow up with calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
[07:06] Ana: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Some ASR errors present in sections — 'kv cache' transcribed as 'k v cash' in quick notes; product names sometimes transcribed. Shared artifacts referenced: security pack (link sent after call), benchmark template (https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/edgecraft), Dedicated pricing worksheet (attached in follow-up).

End of transcript.
